text.content: This kind of problem becomes increasingly common as systems grow. Different teams may develop different components, agents may evolve over time, and new tools may be added to existing workflows. Without a shared communication standard, every change introduces the risk that one component will no longer understand another.

rich_text.plain_text: This kind of problem becomes increasingly common as systems grow. Different teams may develop different components, agents may evolve over time, and new tools may be added to existing workflows. Without a shared communication standard, every change introduces the risk that one component will no longer understand another.

text.content: Communication contracts reduce this risk by creating a clear agreement between components. As long as an agent follows the contract, its internal implementation can change without affecting the rest of the system. One team can improve an agent, replace a database, or introduce a new tool without requiring every other component to be rewritten.

text.content: Contracts also make failures easier to diagnose. When something goes wrong, engineers can quickly check whether the message being sent matches the agreed format. Instead of investigating the entire system, they can focus on the specific point where the contract was violated.

Summary

text.content: Cascadia's support automation does not fall over because any single agent is wrong. It falls over when two agents disagree about the shape of the message they exchange. Structured communication — a contract between components — is what makes multi-agent systems reliable enough to ship.
